question: Can the frozen cone/name/floor Stage carrier remain legible and theatrical across the authority-named 2–5 Character design-stress range without implying Scene cardinality law?
accepted_findings: Sparse two-Character composition may retain large theatrical negative space without inflating Characters into portrait/avatar monuments.
Three- and four-Character layouts can vary spacing while preserving a relational ensemble field and independently readable states.
The five-Character incumbent witness remains legible without converting Characters into cards or dashboard rows.
Human-readable names remain the explicit identity anchor at every tested density.
Listening Characters remain visibly present; speaking, creator selection and current opportunity remain separate meanings.
Narrow layouts compress the same Stage field without horizontal scrolling or substituting a different information architecture.

recursive_audit.fixture_coherence: PASS — Gilligan’s Isle / The Missing Raft family only
recursive_audit.cardinality_boundary: PASS — every 2–5 statement remains design-stress evidence only

explicit_non_authority: 2 and 5 are not minimum/maximum Scene counts; ODR-30 remains open.
No Character membership, entry/exit, addition/removal, scheduling or persistence rule is defined.
No dynamic reflow, animation, cadence or transcript-dependent motion authority is created; Q-DESIGN-02 remains blocked.
Counts outside 2–5 are not ruled out by this study.
PKT-STAGE-CORE-02 remains the Stage anchor; this board does not replace it.
next_boundary: Detail Stage-specific unavailable/interrupted/recovery presentation as a static live-workspace exception study, reusing frozen Phase-1 infrastructure-versus-fiction law without inventing runtime behavior.
approval: APPROVED BY STANDING DIRECTOR DELEGATION — CLEAN RECURSIVE AUDIT.
